summary.text: Regina Ross is the Democratic candidate for Michigan House of Representatives District 4 in the November 3, 2026 general election, against Everett Davis (R); there is no incumbent in the race.
She won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary and has a background in education.

paragraphs.text: Ross was born in Detroit, Michigan.

She received a bachelor's degree in liberal arts with a minor in political science and a master's degree in administration, instructional technology and education from Wayne State University, and a Ph.D. in education from Ashford University.
She taught adult education in the Detroit Public Schools and then moved to childhood education after earning her master's degree.
Ross was a candidate for Detroit City Council District 7 in 2017, when incumbent Gabe Leland defeated her in the general election, and again in 2021, when Fred Durhal III won the general election.
She ran again for the council seat in 2025 and did not advance from the August 5, 2025 primary.
She won the 2026 Democratic primary for the House seat over Krystal Larsosa, Anthony McDonald and Tyus Monroe.
